name: EasyCombIn
headline: The name that closes for Easy Comb-In.
subtitle: Two rounds: the sub-brand name (R1) and the on-pack claims (R2) — Stopping & Closing Power across three audiences.
background: Just For Men is seeking dual placement for Easy Comb-In between the Men's Shave aisle and the Women's Hair Color aisle. The test identifies which title best positions the product — with special attention to Closing Power for the Women's HC set.
objective: Which sub-brand title gives Easy Comb-In the strongest Closing Power? Does the winner hold up across male English, male Spanish and female audiences?
hypothesis: One of the proposed sub-brand titles will have greater closing power than the current “Easy Comb-In Color” title.

methodology.format: 8 digital banners + 8 landing pages — 1 title each

charts.insight: Four challengers out-stop the current name. “Targeted” (2.32%), “Clean-Up” (2.03%), “Easy Touch-Up” (1.91%) and “Quick Fix” (1.90%) all caught significantly more male attention than “Easy Comb-In Color”, which sits near the bottom of the field at 1.51%. Attention alone doesn't decide a rename, though — the next chart shows which of these titles turn that attention into intent.

charts.insight: “Quick Fix” lifts both KPIs. It is the only title significantly above the control on attention and conversion at once, closing at 17.13% among men — right at the benchmark ceiling — while the current name closes below the benchmark floor (8.70% vs. 9.52%). “Precision” converts almost as well (16.67%), but without adding any attention.

charts.title: Stopping Power by title — Men (EN + ES combined) vs. Women
charts.insight: Women stop far more than men. Nearly every title caught more female attention — “Easy Touch-Up” reached a striking 12.82% — which fits a proxy purchase: women notice the product, often while shopping for someone else. The real question is whether all that attention converts, and the next chart answers it.

charts.title: Closing Power by title — Men (EN + ES combined) vs. Women

rows.label: No Mix Hair Color
rows.extra: Best CP of the test with women (directional)

charts.insight: Naming moves men — not the female shopper. For all their extra attention, women converted about three times less than men (3.70% vs. 10.70% pooled, statistically significant): they look, but they don't commit. No title fixed that gap, though “No Mix” came closest at 7.61% — the strongest title with women in the test.

charts.title: Closing Power by title — Male English vs. Male Spanish

rows.label: Touch-Up Hair Color
rows.extra: Collapses in Spanish — only stat. sig. language gap of the test

rows.label: Touch-Up Hair Color
rows.extra: Collapses in Spanish — only stat. sig. language gap of the test

charts.insight: The winners travel across languages. Pooled across all titles there is no meaningful gap between English and Spanish (11.51% vs. 9.82%), and both winning titles hold up on each side — Quick Fix closes at 16.51% in English and 17.76% in Spanish. The exception is “Touch-Up”, which collapses from 13.59% in English to 2.02% in Spanish, the only significant language gap in the test and a caution flag if that title is ever considered. Worth noting: the current name actually leans Spanish (11.63% vs. 6.12%, directional), so any rename should be validated in Spanish-language media first.

charts.title: Closing Power on Hotjar click heat-map landing pages — All audiences
charts.insight: Winning titles focus the click. On the Quick Fix and Precision pages, the heat maps show clicks piling onto a single spot — the Add to Cart button — a sign that visitors arrive already decided. “Easy Touch-Up” tells the opposite story: the most-explored page of the test, with clicks scattered across the pack, the title and the copy, yet one of the lowest closing rates. The current title shows the same diffuse pattern, echoing its below-benchmark conversion. Attention is not intent.

narrative.title: What we tested
narrative.body: Stimuli: 8 sub-brand titles, one constant claim. Eight titles, identical everything else. Same pack, same claim (“Easy no-mix application”), same media — only the sub-brand title changed. 000 · CONTROL Easy Comb-In Color · 001 Targeted Hair Color · 002 Easy Touch-Up Hair Color · 003 Touch-Up Hair Color · 004 Precision Hair Color · 005 Quick Fix Hair Color · 006 Clean-Up Hair Color · 007 No Mix Hair Color.

rounds.outcome: Hypothesis confirmed — two titles beat the control with statistical significance. Recommendation: rename to Quick Fix Hair Color — all three audiences combined, and still the only title that lifts both attention and conversion versus the current name.

charts.title: Stopping Power — Men Total (English + Spanish combined)

rows.label: Just Use Where You Need It

charts.insight: Gray messaging clearly leads among men, with three claims statistically tied for first place: Refresh Just the Gray, Targeted Gray Blending, and Blends Away Early Grays. The numeric leader, Refresh Just the Gray at 2.07%, comes with an asterisk because its performance does not hold up across languages. Encouragingly, all fifteen claims landed inside the IEP benchmark range for Stopping Power, so nothing tested was a true dud.

charts.title: Stopping Power — Male English

rows.label: Just Use Where You Need It

charts.insight: Among English-speaking men, Refresh Just the Gray posts the strongest score at 2.33%, but the deck flags it as a caution because that lead evaporates in Spanish. Targeted Gray Blending sits right behind at 1.93% and, crucially, holds essentially the same score in both languages, which makes it the language-proof pick. The only claim to slip below the benchmark floor here was Multiple Use Hair Color at 1.15%, which interestingly performs noticeably better in Spanish.

charts.title: Stopping Power — Male Spanish

rows.label: Just Use Where You Need It

charts.insight: The Spanish-language picture reshuffles the leaderboard: Controls Early Grays rises to the top at 1.93%, while the English winner Refresh Just the Gray drops to 1.77%, confirming that the numeric leader does not travel across languages. Targeted Gray Blending is the story here, holding at 1.87% versus 1.93% in English with no meaningful gap. On the downside, Refresh Your Temples & Roots falls to 1.11%, just below the benchmark floor, while conditioner claims generally do a bit better with Spanish speakers than English speakers.

charts.title: Stopping Power — Female 30–64

rows.label: Just Use Where You Need It

charts.insight: Women delivered the cleanest result of the round: Controls Early Grays stands alone at 2.52%, statistically above every other top-tier claim and the only score in the entire test to clear the top of the IEP benchmark band. There is no ambiguity or tie to argue about here, which is rare in these tests. The rest of the female leaderboard also runs noticeably hotter than the men's, echoing the pattern seen in Round 1.

charts.title: Where Women Out-Index Men Most (R2, secondary detail)
charts.insight: Across two rounds testing two different variables, sub-brand naming and now on-pack claims, women have consistently paused more than men on Easy Comb-In creative, and both rounds reached statistical significance. In Round 2 the pooled gap was 1.86% for women versus 1.65% for men, with the widest individual spreads on Controls Early Grays and Targeted Gray Coverage. This is starting to look like a durable, brand-level pattern rather than a quirk of any single test.

narrative.title: What we set out to answer
narrative.body: This round asked which of fifteen on-pack claims captures the most attention across three audiences, so the team can recommend what actually goes on the physical product box. Unlike Round 1, which tested sub-brand titles, this test isolated the claim text itself: same pack, same media, same audiences, with only the banner copy rotating. The hypothesis was that claims naming a specific, targeted benefit, like gray-blending precision or early-gray action, would outperform generic usage-flexibility or ingredient-only claims. Importantly, this round measured Stopping Power only, with no Closing Power read.

narrative.title: The top claim doesn't travel
narrative.body: Refresh Just the Gray was the numeric leader among men overall at 2.07%, but the language cut told a different story: it scored 2.33% in English and collapsed to 1.77% in Spanish. Targeted Gray Blending, by contrast, held essentially steady at 1.93% in English and 1.87% in Spanish, making it the language-proof option among the statistically tied leaders. When a claim is going on a box that both English and Spanish speakers will see, that consistency matters more than a fragile numeric edge.

narrative.title: Women rally around one clear claim
narrative.body: The female audience produced the single strongest result of the entire round: Controls Early Grays reached 2.52%, standing statistically above every other top-tier claim and clearing the top of the IEP benchmark, the only claim in the test to do so. Where the men's results came in clusters and ties, women converged decisively on one message. It suggests the early-gray-control framing has real pull with this audience.

narrative.title: Women pause more than men, twice now
narrative.body: Project Compass now has the same directional finding from two consecutive rounds built on completely different variables. In Round 2, women pooled at 1.86% Stopping Power against 1.65% for men, and both rounds' gaps were statistically significant. Since this held first for sub-brand naming and now for on-pack claims, it reads as a reinforced, brand-level pattern: women consistently stop for Easy Comb-In creative more than the men the product is aimed at.

narrative.title: Conditioner claims open a diversification path
narrative.body: Outside the gray-messaging territory, the ingredient and care claims held their own, with Includes Nourishing Conditioner landing in the men's top five at 1.74%. That gives the brand a genuinely different story to tell on-pack alongside a gray claim, rather than stacking three variations of the same message. It is a useful reminder that the box does not have to say the same thing three ways.

rounds.outcome: The round settled the question it was built for: gray messaging is the territory that stops men, but the safest single claim for the box is Targeted Gray Blending, which ties statistically for the top men's score at 1.90% and shows no English/Spanish gap, unlike the fragile numeric leader Refresh Just the Gray. Every one of the fifteen claims landed within the IEP benchmark, and among women one claim, Controls Early Grays at 2.52%, stood decisively above everything else and above the benchmark itself. The test also reconfirmed, for the second consecutive round, that women pause for this creative significantly more than men.

learnings: Women convert far below men. They pause on the banners nearly twice as often, yet close about three times less (3.70% vs. 10.70%, statistically significant) — a classic proxy-purchase pattern: they notice the product, but the decision isn't theirs. No title fixed it, so the way to reach them is on-pack, not through the name.

The best name is “Quick Fix Hair Color”. It was the only title significantly above the control on both attention and conversion — closing at 12.42% across all audiences and 17.13% among men, where the current name falls below the benchmark floor. “Precision Hair Color” is a validated alternative: statistically tied on conversion, but without the attention lift.

Spanish and English agree on the winner. There is no overall language gap (11.51% vs. 9.82%) and both winning titles hold their numbers in each language. The one caution is “Touch-Up”, which collapses in Spanish (13.59% → 2.02%) — the only significant language gap of the test.

A numeric winner is not automatically the right winner. Refresh Just the Gray topped the men's combined table at 2.07%, but its English score of 2.33% fell to 1.77% in Spanish, so a claim destined for a bilingual shelf needs to pass a language check before it earns the box.

Targeted, benefit-specific gray claims outperformed generic flexibility and ingredient-only claims among men, broadly confirming the round's hypothesis. The top of the men's table was dominated by gray-blending and early-gray-action messaging, while claims like Multiple Use Hair Color sat at the bottom and even dipped below the benchmark floor in English.

Women responded far more decisively than men, rallying around Controls Early Grays at 2.52%, the only score in the test to clear the benchmark ceiling. Combined with the pooled gap of 1.86% versus 1.65%, this is the second round in a row where women showed higher Stopping Power on Easy Comb-In creative, making it a durable brand-level pattern rather than a one-off.

Conditioner and care claims are a viable second story for the pack. Includes Nourishing Conditioner reached the men's top five at 1.74% and performed even better in Spanish, showing the brand can diversify its on-pack messaging beyond gray coverage without sacrificing attention.
recommendations: Rename to “Quick Fix Hair Color”. It delivered the test's highest Closing Power (12.42% across all audiences, statistically above the control) while also lifting attention (2.45%), and it wins with men in both languages (16.51% EN · 17.76% ES).

Keep “Precision Hair Color” as the validated alternative. It ties Quick Fix on conversion (12.33%) and is equally language-proof, but its attention stays at control level — it converts without drawing extra eyes.

Speak to the female shopper with “No Mix” on the pack. It was the strongest title with women (7.61%, directional) and third overall; rather than renaming for her, elevate it as a highlighted on-pack claim for the Women's Hair Color aisle.

Make Targeted Gray Blending the primary claim on the box. It is statistically tied for the top Stopping Power score among men at 1.90%, and unlike the raw numeric leader it shows no significant gap between English and Spanish, which makes it the more reliable choice for a claim that has to work across both languages.

Add Includes Nourishing Conditioner as the secondary claim. This is a deliberate shift out of gray-coverage territory into an ingredient and care benefit, and it earned a respectable, statistically competitive top-five score among men at 1.74%, giving the pack a genuinely different second message.

Round out the box with Touch Up Your Temples & Roots as the third claim. At 1.68% among men it is statistically even with the conditioner claim, shows no English/Spanish gap, and opens a third distinct territory, precision touch-up, so the three claims cover gray coverage, care ingredients, and application precision without repeating themselves. A near-duplicate fourth option, Blends Away Early Grays, was deliberately set aside to keep the territories distinct, and all three picks should be treated as directional recommendations.

name: Mustache & Beard
headline: The claim that wins the shelf.
subtitle: A claims-attention test for Just For Men Mustache & Beard Color - 31 claims, three audiences, one KPI: Stopping Power.
background: Just For Men is seeking dual placement for Mustache & Beard Color between the Men's Shave aisle and the Women's Hair Color aisle. A test is needed to discover which claims best position the product, to inform an update to the current on-pack claims.
objective: Which claims resonate best with the target audiences?
success_criteria: Stopping Power (this test does not measure Closing Power). No hypothesis was defined for this round — the read is exploratory across claims and audiences.

narrative.title: Who we're talking to
narrative.body: Three segments, same interest criteria — split by gender and language to see whether claims travel across all three. MEN · EN: Male, age 30–64, interests Hair coloring, Hair products, Just For Men, or Men's grooming products (11.3 – 13.3 MM Meta estimated size). MEN · ES: Male, age 30–64, Spanish — same interests, AND speaks Spanish (2.3 – 2.7 MM). WOMEN: Female, age 30–64, same interests (24.3 – 28.6 MM). Combined addressable reach ≈ 38–44MM across the three segments.

narrative.title: What we tested
narrative.body: Stimuli: 31 claims across 6 themes. Same pack, same brush — only the on-pack claim changed. Example creative: Banner 005 · “3 easy steps”. EASE OF APPLICATION (6): 001 Easy Brush-In Application · 005 3 easy steps · 006 No Mix, Hassle-free Application · 007 Designed for Easy, at Home Use · 014 Use what you need, save the rest for later · 015 Up to 3 uses: Reusable for Future Use. PRECISION & BRUSH TOOL (6): 002 Precision brush for sideburns and temples · 003 Precision brush for root touchups · 004 New Precision brush for touch ups · 019 Built for precise facial hair application · 020 Precision control for detailed application · 021 Designed for neat, targeted results. MOISTURE & NOURISHMENT (10): 008 Moisturizes Hair with Aloe and Coconut Oil · 009 Infused with Aloe & Coconut Oil for Softer Feeling Hair · 010 Aloe & Coconut Oil to Help Hydrate as it Colors · 022 Helps facial hair feel softer as it covers grays · 023 Moisture minded gray coverage for mustache & beard · 024 Facial hair color with a more nourished feel · 025 Supports a softer, more conditioned beard · 026 Designed to leave hair feeling healthier after coloring · 027 Helps reduce dryness with Aloe & Coconut Oil · 028 Smooth, conditioned feel with Aloe & Coconut Oil. GENTLE / HEALTHIER FORMULA (3): 011 No Ammonia, no PPD · 012 Healthier-looking hair · 013 Gentle Formula Specifically Designed for Facial Hair. COLOR RESULT & LONGEVITY (5): 016 Won't Wash Out – Lasts Until Gray Grows Back · 017 Natural-looking color for mustache & beard · 029 Designed for coarse facial hair · 030 A simple routine for beard color refresh · 031 Ideal for mustache, beard and sideburns. TARGETED COLOR TECHNOLOGY (1): 018 Targeted color specifically designed for facial hair.

rounds.outcome: With two claims already proven across every audience and four of the strongest results specifically with men, this set gives the box both safety and strength, enough range to fill front and back without repeating a single claim.

learnings: Two themes dominate the men's top 10: Moisture & nourishment (Aloe & Coconut Oil) and Ease of application each account for 3 of the top 10.
Only two claims land in every audience's top 10: “3 easy steps” and “Natural-looking color for mustache & beard”. Everything else is audience-specific.

“Aloe & Coconut Oil” repeats in 3 of the men's top 10; the strongest is “Smooth, conditioned feel with Aloe & Coconut Oil” (1.88%); “Infused with Aloe & Coconut Oil for Softer Feeling Hair” (1.70%) and “Aloe & Coconut Oil to Help Hydrate as it Colors” (1.55%) are equally valid alternates.
All 31 claims fall within the IEP benchmark band [1.18% – 2.48%] — the read ranks relative performance, not pass/fail. Pool averages: Men (EN+ES) 1.42% · Men EN 1.46% · Men ES 1.37% · Women 1.74%.
recommendations: Anchor the pack with the two universal claims: “3 easy steps” and “Natural-looking color for mustache & beard” — the only two that made every audience's top ten.
Add the strongest men's claims for punch: “Precision brush for root touchups” (1.89%) and “Smooth, conditioned feel with Aloe & Coconut Oil” (1.88%), the top performers with men in both languages.

Round out with ease of application: “Up to 3 uses: Reusable for Future Use” (1.82%) and “Easy Brush-In Application” (1.73%) complete a six-claim set that fills front and back of the box without repeating a message.

If more moisture claims are needed, “Infused with Aloe & Coconut Oil for Softer Feeling Hair” (1.70%) and “Aloe & Coconut Oil to Help Hydrate as it Colors” (1.55%) are validated alternates from the same family.
